note: Captured runs. Each entry is one rfd4-generate run exported by workflow/export_playback.py. Until a run is captured this file lists what is planned, and the pages say so rather than pretending.

quickstart.title: The documentation's own example
quickstart.what: The binder from the RFD4 quickstart, run on the input file that ships with the repo. It is here as the canary: it proves the install works and gives us frames to look at before any GPU time goes on a real target.

planned.command: rfd4-generate inputs=quickstart.yaml out_dir=./runs/quickstart num_replicates=8 seed=1234 metrics_tags='[design]' generation.args.save_trajectory_every=2 generation.args.bb_ca_only_trajectories=false generation.args.dump_noisy_trajectories=true

motif.title: Scaffold a motif
motif.what: Three residues held in place while the model builds a protein around them. The classic lesson, and the one where the contig language earns its keep.

planned.command: rfd4-generate inputs=motif.yaml out_dir=./runs/motif num_replicates=16 seed=1234 metrics_tags='[design]' generation.args.save_trajectory_every=2 generation.args.bb_ca_only_trajectories=false

binder_3evg.title: A binder against 3EVG
binder_3evg.what: Brian's own dengue-2 NS5 methyltransferase, the same target the BindCraft2 site uses, so the two tools can be compared on one structure.

planned.command: rfd4-generate inputs=binder_3evg.yaml out_dir=./runs/binder_3evg num_replicates=32 seed=1234 metrics_tags='[design]' generation.args.save_trajectory_every=2 generation.args.bb_ca_only_trajectories=false
